To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the scintillation of a partially coherent beam in a strongly turbulent atmosphere saturates to a constant of 1.0, and (2) the scintillations are a function of the degree of spatial coherence of the beam and the strength of the turbulence.
the scintillations index for a partially coherent source saturates to a constant, which depends upon the degree of source coherence, and the scintillating irradiance pattern is Gaussian distributed.
the scintil­ lation index of a partially coherent wave propagating in a strong turbulence medium saturates to unity and that the rate of saturation depends on the source coherence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation of partially coherent light through a turbulent medium.
the propagation of partially coherent light through an extremely strong turbulent medium, with the emphasis on irradiance fluctuations.
the propagation of partially coherent radiation in turbulent atmospheres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as the degree of coherence decreases, the scintillation becomes more severe.
the scintillations are completely independent of the source coherence and the medium turbulence.
in the limit of extremely strong turbulence the scintillations are not affected by the degree of coherence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scintillations index for a partially coherent source approaches unity in the limit of extremely strong turbulence.
the scintillations saturate to a constant of 1 + 2ρ2s/σ2, where σ2 is the variance of the log-amplitude fluctuations of the wave.
the irradiance scintillation index is a function of the ratio of the coherence radius of the source to the Fresnel zone radius.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scintillations are not affected by the degree of coherence, but only by its spatial distribution.
, in the case of strong turbulence, the scintillation indices are not dependent on the source coherence properties, but are dependent on the ratio of the source diameter to the Fried parameter, r0.
the scintil­ lation index is independent of the coherence of the source, and is a function only of the turbulence parameters and the ratio of the Fresnel number to the scintillation number.
